A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DeltaProduct. All 19 pages of v1 and 21 pages of v3, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison. Renamed and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original DeltaProduct experiments on group state-tracking, formal languages, and language modeling, including scaling and length-extrapolation analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results, reports revised formal-language scores, and adds a runtime experiment in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The multiple key/value projections, sequential gradient updates, Householder products, and inference procedure remain unchanged. Gated DeltaProduct already appears in v1; v3's Appendix B explicitly documents its equations rather than introducing a new component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four permutation groups, three formal-language tasks, FineWeb training data, language-modeling benchmarks, and four long-context evaluation datasets. The added runtime sweep changes experimental procedures rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained in the corresponding formal-language and language-modeling comparisons, including both DeltaNet eigenvalue ranges and the matched-parameter language-modeling baseline. Newly discussed related methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v1 Appendix C.2.1 specifies one head of dimension 128 for all DeltaProduct/DeltaNet formal-language tasks; v3 Appendix E.2.1 specifies 12 heads of dimension 32 for bracketed arithmetic. This is a reported setting revision, without establishing reruns. Appendix C also introduces a single-layer runtime protocol spanning 64–8192 tokens and nh=1–4.

E4.justification: v3 Appendix C adds runtime scaling analysis across sequence lengths and Householder counts. The existing depth/head comparisons, eigenvalue-range experiments, rotation/PCA analysis, training curves, and length-extrapolation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The new runtime study reports 200 iterations, averaging, and a three-iteration burn-in. This adds repeated-measurement information, not additional training seeds. Formal-language results retain the best-of-three-seeds reporting practice, without new confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: The bracketed-arithmetic results and associated averages are revised throughout v1 Table 1/v3 Table 2, materially narrowing the reported advantage. DeltaProduct4[-1,1] changes from 0.460 to 0.342 on that task and from 0.778 to 0.739 overall; DeltaNet[-1,1] changes from 0.253 to 0.281 on that task. These accompany changed reported settings, so they do not establish same-setting performance changes. v3 also adds runtime measurements; the main language-modeling table retains its scores.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 newly specifies a finite-precision linear RNN, while its construction and proof remain essentially unchanged. Appendix E.1 adds geometric group assertions, including an incorrect identification of full dodecahedral symmetry with S5. The identical-key lemma and central Householder derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: tunable expressivity through Householder products, improved state-tracking and language modeling, stronger length extrapolation, and two-layer DeltaNet expressivity for dihedral groups. The revised title and explicit highlighting of the gated variant do not materially change their scope.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix E.1 expand the geometric explanation into actions on cube diagonals and inscribed cubes, including a new S5 interpretation. The existing rotation/PCA interpretation, forgetting hypothesis, and limitations concerning computational cost and multilayer expressivity remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly specifies the scalar gate's sigmoid parameterization and explicit gated transition equations. Appendix C documents timing hardware, bfloat16 precision, batch size, model dimensions, compilation, and measurement procedure. The existing training pipeline and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 substantially expands positioning against concurrent fixed-point RNN approaches and earlier structured, orthogonal recurrent models, including Householder, rotation, and Kronecker constructions. It explains complementary approaches and distinctions from these predecessors, beyond merely adding citations. Bibliographic publication updates are separate from this substantive expansion.

P1.justification: v3 revises the title, author-credit information, publication headers, and portions of the background, method explanation, and analysis prose. It adds dedicated gating and runtime appendices and adjusts cross-references, while preserving the six main sections and most of the narrative.

P2.justification: v3 adds a transition-matrix schematic, a bracketed-arithmetic summary plot, a runtime plot, and a cube illustration. It moves the complete formal-language table from the main text to the appendix and substantially rearranges surrounding displays. The new arithmetic plot redisplays revised table results; retained figures are matched across relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v3 supports the runtime-scaling assertion with measurements and improves implementation documentation and positioning against closely related research. However, Appendix E.1 introduces a mathematical error by identifying full dodecahedral symmetry with S5: central inversion preserves each inscribed cube and does not supply the claimed odd permutations. These useful additions coexist with a substantive new error in the theoretical explanation, leaving the net overall quality change uncertain.
